title: It Was A Pleasure Waiting, Mr.Godot; Brendan Gall Riffs On Beckett's Iconic

display_heading.headline: It Was A Pleasure Waiting, Mr.Godot
display_heading.deck: Brendan Gall Riffs On Beckett's Iconic Non-Visitor With A Dapper And Clever Star

contact_edits.before: Actually, the play has yet a third level, as police-procedural, real or parodied, but here it speedily runs out of gas. There's an offstage figure referred to as Jimmy Nicknames, a sort of Godot's Godot; but if Godot was obscure, Jimmy is simply confusing. The play moves towards an apocalyptic finish that it simply hasn't earned. Like Beckett's first postwar, Cold War audiences, we bring our own existential dread into the theatre with us; but where his play distilled it into something new and personal, this one just plays with what we already know. People said the same thing 40 years ago about Tom Stoppard's Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead, another self-confessed Beckett knock-off, but one that also had the thickly populated landscape of Hamlet to draw from. It kept strictly and fruitfully to the rules of the Shakespearean plot. Gall has to invent his own, which proves paradoxically constricting. Also, he isn't as funny as Stoppard. But he's plenty funny, and the play, his first at full-length, is the most scintillating debut we've had this season. - Alias Godot runs through June 1 at the Tarragon. Call 416-531-1827 for ticket information.
